codexVersion: codex-cli 0.167.0 (native aarch64-apple-darwin, npm wrapper execve's into it)
setup: Throwaway Codex TUI in a scratch git project outside Herdr, private pty, fake HC_* variables (no route to any Herdr core), -s read-only -a never. A project SessionStart hook that only logged its input was trusted through Codex's own hook review; both trust entries were removed afterwards and ~/.codex/config.toml returned to its exact prior SHA256.

assertions.label: SessionStart fires at the first submitted prompt, not at TUI start
SessionStart payload carries session_id, transcript_path, cwd and source (startup, then clear after /clear)
Hook process inherits HC_TERMINAL_ID, HC_SCOPE and HC_TERMINAL_SOCKET from Codex's environment
Hook process parent is the Codex process itself
session_id equals the ID in 'codex resume <id>' printed on exit
The transcript file exists before the hook runs; its session_meta header has id == session_id, parent_thread_id null, source cli, thread_source user
Open files cannot identify the current session: after /clear Codex holds two thread-writer locks and two session files
Codex has separate SubagentStart/SubagentStop hook events (binary strings); subagent SessionStart not exercised because the plan's usage limit was reached

exitMessage: To continue this session, run: codex resume 01a1b4cc-c4d4-7980-970a-411ea9d001e7
limits: The prompt hit the account usage limit, so no model turn completed; hooks fired regardless.
hc label from inside a Herdr terminal is not exercised here; the private native harness proves it.
